The 2025 Berlin ePrix, known for sponsorship reasons as the 2025 Hankook Berlin E-Prix, was a pair of Formula E electric car races held at the Tempelhof Airport Street Circuit at Tempelhof Airport in the outskirts of Berlin, Germany on 12 and 13 July 2025. It served as the 11th and 12th rounds of the 2024–25 Formula E season, and marked the 11th edition of the Berlin ePrix, the only event to have featured in every season of the Formula E championship.

Background

[edit]

Oliver Rowland leads into Berlin with 172 points and a 69-point lead over Pascal Wehrlein. Followed by António Félix da Costa and Taylor Barnard.[1]

Driver changes

[edit]

Two drivers would miss the Berlin E-Prix because of a schedule conflict with the FIA World Endurance Championship's 6 Hours of São Paulo. Mahindra Racing's Nyck de Vries would be replaced by Felipe Drugovich.[2] Nissan's reserve driver Sérgio Sette Câmara would replace Norman Nato.[3]

Race one

Qualification

[edit]

Qualification was originally scheduled to take place at 11:20 AM on 12 July.[4] However, due to adverse weather conditions, the session was postponed to start at 12:00 PM. Due to time constraints, the duels were not held and the group stages were used to decide the starting grid.[5] Because of this the three extra points were not awarded to the driver who obtained pole position.

Notes

[edit]
  1. ^ 39 planned laps + 2 added laps
  2. ^ 38 planned laps + 3 added laps
  3. ^ Wehrlein received a 3-place grid drop for causing a collision with Da Costa in Free Practice 1.
  4. ^ Drugovich received a 20-place grid drop for changing his gearbox in excess of the limit.
  5. ^ Cassidy was given a 20-place grid drop for changing his inverters in excess of the limit at the previous race in Jakarta.
  6. ^ Buemi received a 40-place grid drop for changing his MGU and MCU components in excess of the limit.
  7. ^ Da Costa was given a 5-second time penalty for causing a collision with Hughes.
  8. ^ Sette Câmara was given a 10-second time penalty for causing a collision with Beckmann.
  9. ^ Rowland received a 5-place grid drop for causing a collision with Vandoorne in Saturday's race at Berlin.
  10. ^ Günther received a 3-place grid drop for failing to respect the black and orange flag in Free Practice 3.
  11. ^ Sette Câmara received a 3-place grid drop for not following red flag procedures in Free Practice 3.
  12. ^ Müller was given a 10-second time penalty for causing a collision with Bird.
